journal_article.label: Peer-Reviewed Journal Article
journal_article.tone: Objective, concise, cautious in interpretation, precise in methodology.
journal_article.person_policy: Prefer passive or active first-person plural ('we') only for author actions; avoid second-person 'you'.

tense_guidance.abstract: Past tense for methods/results; present tense for general truths and main conclusions.
tense_guidance.introduction: Present tense for established knowledge; present perfect for prior literature; past/present for this study's aim.
tense_guidance.results: Simple past tense for observations; present tense when referring to figures/tables ('Fig. 1 shows').
tense_guidance.discussion: Past tense for study findings; hedged present/modal verbs for interpretations.

thesis.label: Master's / Doctoral Thesis
thesis.tone: Formal, thorough, structurally explicit, consistent across chapters.
thesis.person_policy: Prefer 'this study / this chapter / 本文 / 本章' over 'I / 我'.

tense_guidance.general: Consistent chapter-level tense; avoid abrupt voice shifts.

grant_proposal.label: Research Grant Proposal (NSFC / NIH / NSF)
grant_proposal.tone: Persuasive yet scientifically rigorous; clear problem-gap-hypothesis-feasibility logic without exaggerated hype.
grant_proposal.person_policy: First-person plural ('we' / '本项目' / '申请团队') acceptable and clear.

rebuttal.label: Peer-Review Response / Rebuttal Letter
rebuttal.tone: Respectful, appreciative, direct, evidence-anchored; explicitly state where revisions were made.

tense_guidance.actions_taken: Present perfect / past tense ('We have revised Section 3.2...').

abstract.label: Standalone Academic Abstract
abstract.tone: High information density, zero fluff, self-contained abbreviations, strict hedge preservation.
